Test Constancy of Markov Transition Probabilities across Time

Source: R/05_ht.R
test_const.Rd

Test whether independent Markov trajectories share a transition matrix that is constant across observation times, using the Pearson test in Section 3.2 of Anderson and Goodman (1957), Equation (3.8).

Usage

test_const(x)

Arguments

x

An atomic matrix with one independent trajectory per row and common observation times in columns. At least two rows and three columns are required. Missing values are not allowed. Validated by the internal validate_trajectories() helper. A single vector is not sufficient for this test.

Value

An object of class htest, with components statistic (named X-squared), parameter (degrees of freedom), p.value, method, and data.name. Additional components are estimate (the pooled transition matrix), and observed and expected (arrays indexed by source state, destination state, and transition time). State order is first appearance when reading paths row by row.

Details

Write \(T = \mathrm{ncol}(x)-1\) for the number of transition times and \(m\) for the number of observed states. Let \(N_{ij}(t)\) count paths making transition \(i\to j\) at time \(t\), and let \(N_i(t-1)=\sum_j N_{ij}(t)\). Under the null, the pooled estimate is $$\widehat p_{ij} = \frac{\sum_t N_{ij}(t)}{\sum_t N_i(t-1)}.$$ The statistic is $$X^2 = \sum_{i,j,t} \frac{(N_{ij}(t)-N_i(t-1)\widehat p_{ij})^2} {N_i(t-1)\widehat p_{ij}}.$$ Its asymptotic null distribution is chi-squared with \(m(m-1)(T-1)\) degrees of freedom. The alternative allows a different transition matrix at each time. Paths must be independent, but observations within a path need not be independent. The approximation is for increasing numbers of paths with fixed \(m\) and \(T\), positive transition probabilities, and growing origin counts at every transition time.

This implementation requires at least two observed states, a positive origin count at every transition time for every state, and positive pooled counts for every ordered state pair. Empty margins cause an error rather than an automatic change to the paper's degrees of freedom. A warning is issued when any expected cell count is below five. No continuity correction is applied. Reject at a chosen significance level when the p-value is below that level. This tests time homogeneity, not equality of the initial and stationary distributions.

References

Anderson, T. W., and Goodman, L. A. (1957). Statistical Inference about Markov Chains. The Annals of Mathematical Statistics, 28(1), 89–110. doi:10.1214/aoms/1177707039 . Section 3.2, especially Equations (3.6) and (3.8).

See also

test_prob(), fit(), stats::chisq.test()

Examples

# Repeated copies of all binary paths of length three.
paths <- as.matrix(expand.grid(start = c("a", "b"),
                              middle = c("a", "b"), end = c("a", "b")))
x <- paths[rep(seq_len(nrow(paths)), each = 10), ]
test_const(x)
#> 
#> 	Anderson-Goodman test of constant transition probabilities
#> 
#> data:  x
#> X-squared = 0, df = 2, p-value = 1
#> sample estimates:
#>     to
#> from   a   b
#>    a 0.5 0.5
#>    b 0.5 0.5
#>
